segments.text: Say for example, we are implementing food safety and standards properly.
Say milk, we are tackling one of the major issues of milk and milk products.

In Maharashtra, I am told, though I cannot have scientific data, but whatever I'm hearing from districts and villages and corporations is that the milk purchase price by dairies and the consumers has gone up.
by 10 to 20 rupees per litre in last three months' time.
Now, there can be multiple causes to it.
I'm not saying this is the only component.
This definitely is a one-contributory factor where the income of farmers is increasing.
So on the one hand, income of farmers will increase.
Productivity and standard of living in the long run will go up for farmers.
On the other hand, people will get safe food.
Ultimately, health will improve.
So it's actually a win-win situation for the people.
I think your point you're saying in the farming sector.
I take your point that you're saying therefore that this is a drive to ensure compliance and be improved the quality of public health above all else.
But I have a point here.
You see in your pharma crackdown all the focus is on the food.
Very few are focusing on your pharma drug crackdown.

Seizures in Maharashtra alone between June and August twenty twenty six since you've taken over eleven point four one crore of these drugs have been seized in twenty five twenty six the entire year just over thirty point six crores were seized.
It means in three months.
You've seized almost as was seized in the last year.
I again come back to food.
In terms of suspension of licenses or notices sent, you've sent far more in these three months than was sent in the entire year.
Does that mean that the Food and Drug Administration, before you took over, was not functioning, turning a blind eye to this?
And therefore, this is a wake-up call.
What you have done in the last 90 days suggests to me that nothing was being done in the past, or not enough, certainly, was being done in the past.
I believe that rather I when I stepped in this position the systems were in place.
So it did not have stepped in a vacuum.
People have done work since 2011 or before that since this act came into existence system were needed to be placed.
Whether it's digitizing system whether it's officers to be appointed whether the officers to be set up.
And particularly, this law being implemented since 2011, this new compliance also required an approach change among the food business operators and in my offices.
So that has been there.
So we are working furthering the cause.
It's not as if I have just started from Hakim and created everything.
The system did exist.
That's why we are doing.
We still need improvement.
We will do that.
Now the scale can be different.
I mean we can discuss debate whatever we may say.
But people have contributed.
It's not just me.
Now why does it has.
One of the reasons what you directly and indirectly asking is why sudden rise.
Now, Southern Rise, I believe that when I joined, we created something called a mission mode approach.
And we have decided very, very clear mission.
Mission is safe food, safe drugs, safe Maratha, I have said earlier on your channel also.
So this is a mission, and we have defined very, very clear defined strategy also.
What has happened is there is a clarity of purpose, there is a commitment.
You're saying clarity of purpose, there's a commitment, there's a mission approach.
Can I for a moment turn to the flip side because the flip side is
that you've been accused by the Bombay High Court, meaning the FDA, you're going overboard.
The court has said imposed a five lakh cost on you for not restoring a Pune shops license.
Once they said you're using a sword to kill a mosquito.
Then they said that you have a pedantic view and cleared the reopening of five eateries at the Mumbai Cricket Association premises.
Then on 30th August, the same court says, tired of scolding your officers.
The point I'm making, the court seemed to already, the section of the court thinks that Mr. Munde is going overboard.
What will you tell those who say, are you going overboard in this mission mode of yours?
Absolutely not.
I am bound by as a public servant by rules regulations processes.
We are following that.
Now this what your statement you are saying are basically might have come in an argument.
It had not.
It is not a part of order except this five lakh rupees fine which was imposed.
for which we are actually availing the remedy.
We are examining whether it can be SLP in the Supreme Court or it can be review.
So we are examining that and we are taking result to that because we believe that in that case also we did follow the due process.
We did follow the law.
Our officers have not erred in that.
Now second point what you are saying whenever
court makes some observations.
We do take it seriously.
And if there are some errors, either in the process or application of law or interpretation of law, we do take seriously and we rectify wherever they are.
But by and large, we have seen that we have not gone overboard.
In case of some MCA, what you are talking about, court had actually given some direction.
And the direction was that my designated officer or assistant commissioner
had to pass an order on a particular point on which order was passed, but not on that exactly point.
That's what the court ordered that way.
And then court told that issue a notice, issue the order on that point and take further call.
So we are following that process.
So it's not as if we are not following the court order.
But very clearly, I believe that we are not going overboard.
We are the process.
Now you're saying due process.
But could you have given maybe warnings to some of these establishments which have been long long running establishments.
You've actually suspended or temporarily or otherwise licenses of top clubs of restaurants that have been in Mumbai for more than 50 years like K. Rustam.
You've now gone to is gone.
Could you have given them warnings.
before you suspended them because their reputation gets damaged.
So what would you tell those restaurant owners who say that because of Mr. Munde, we are going to lose business, our reputation is getting damaged.
So there are two issues to it.
One, I just give you a data of 12,000 inspections, suspensions are only 600.
and there are notices more than 5000 improvement notices.
So, look at the percentage will come to around 50 percent inspections where around 50 percent establishment got notices.
So, the your answer lies in the data.
So the answer is that we are giving the notices wherever they are needed.

And we are taking action with their cases where suspension is immediately needed, where it is directly affecting the public health, because we have found the unsafe environment there where the food was prepared, which is likely to affect adversely the public health.
Then and there only we have gone for fourth with suspension that law is very clear about it.
Law allows for designated officer to take this call.
And that's where we have done that.
That is first part.
Secondly, we are not here to tarnish anybody's reputation.
Here we are here to look at whether public health is being compromised or not.
We are talking about reputation of one restaurant or employment of a restaurant or hotel or any other establishment for that matter.
What about the consumers which are consuming eating and getting ill or sick because of that.
So that is a prime concern for us.
That is our objective.
So mission mode.
is not the ultimate goal.
Mission is to achieve the larger goal of public health, as I told you.
That's our mandate.
That's what we are trying to do it.
So it's not about tarnishing any image, damaging any business.
They have to comply with.
And if they are in this business, say, for example, 50 years or 100 years, there is more reason that they should be aware of this and comply with this.
I take your point, but what happens if they... Sir, I take your point, Mr. Munde.
I take your point.
But what if I'm a small street corner business selling what a power of power.
I mean Mumbai is known for its street corner food.
I as a consumer I'm going knowing fully where I'm eating street corner food.
Now you're are you going to those street corner food joints and closing them down.
People are going to lose employment.
I think.
So it's not, again, losing employment.
Please understand, they are also registered with us.
They are supposed to be registered with us.
They have to follow the regulations.
And if you have seen, as you said, Vada Pavwala or some Bhujiawala or something else, they are also improved.
Look at they are not using most of them.
I can show 100%.
But by and large, they are providing the food, the Vada Pavw, in a food-grade material.
Not in the newspaper.
They're also cleaning it.
Now there are also many of them have stopped using reused oil, which is prohibited.
So it's not something big or small.
Rules are there.
And the rules are meant for both food business operator, what they have to share.
And ultimately, the objective is because you will get the business if people are healthy and they come to eat you.
If people become sick, they're not going to come to you.
And that's not your objective or the government objective.
Just a reference here, Rajdeep.
There is a WHO report, which is published just in June 2026, which states that there are more than 200 foodborne diseases.
Out of these 200, and there is a huge data, I'll give you the data of 2011.

I remember, 2011 data of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, which says that because of the unsafe and substandard food which is consumed, more GDP loss of one lakh plus crore rupees was lost.
If you take the data of Maharashtra for the same year, more than 2000 crore GDP are lost because of this one, football diseases and things.
Are you not going to think about all these things?
So please understand, we are here to promote genuine businesses.
We have to understand health as an issue.
And we have to understand.
Last point I am making.
Just last one.
Just a second.
It's an important point.
We have been speaking about availability of food and nutrition of food.
That's important.
That's essential.
Today, we have to speak about food safety, also equally important issue, and that's what we are working on.

So I want to therefore in conclusion simple answer a lot of people are supporting you celebrating you citizens are telling me whenever I go to Mumbai to kind of Monday someone who's setting a real example of what one bureaucrat and his team can do to simple question you've had 25 transfers over your career.
And I met a minister here in Delhi who said, you know, this Tukaram Munde, he's a real troublemaker.
He should be taught a lesson.
Do you have a full support of the Maharashtra government, of the Fadnavis government, of the BMC in what you're doing?
Are they fully supporting you, or are you worried that you'll be transferred out soon?
See, as Sandeep, as I said, it's a prerogative of the government.
Because of government support, I am posted here.
Otherwise, I would not be posted here.
It's the authority of the government whether to post, where to post, when to post.
So that's not my jurisdiction.
That's not my authority.
So it's the government which will take a call.
And as I said earlier also, if I keep thinking about my posting, I'll not be able to work.
I should be doing the job or role which is assigned to me.
That's what I'm trying to do.
My final question, everyone calling you the real-life Singham.
Have you become a celebrity and has that gone to your head in any way?
Or you still see yourself as a bureaucrat enforcing the law?
Absolutely not.
Not gone to your head?
I have objection to this bureaucrat.
I am a public servant or a civil servant.
It will not go.
Basically, I am here right now working as a FDI commissioner, as a public servant.
I'll keep doing as long as I'm a public servant.
